---
title: "Architecture"
---

Autosprint's Python package is organised as a strict **layered architecture**.
Modules are grouped into eight sub-packages, and imports may only point *down*
the stack. The rule is enforced automatically by
[import-linter](https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/) (see `[tool.importlinter]`
in `pyproject.toml`) — a contract that fails CI and the pre-commit hooks if any
module imports from a layer above it.

## Layered package diagram

A layer may import from **any** layer below it, never from one above. The arrows
show the adjacency of the stack; the dashed back-edges are the runtime path
(each sprint loops), not import dependencies.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-layers
%%| fig-cap: "The eight package layers. Imports flow strictly downward; any layer may use any layer beneath it."
flowchart TD
  app["app<br>orchestrator · cli · init · how_far<br><i>entry points & user surface</i>"]
  phases["phases<br>plan · implement · test<br><i>the PIT phases</i>"]
  reporting["reporting<br>run_log · banners<br><i>observability & presentation</i>"]
  infra["infra<br>dispatch · git_ops · test_runners · db · stop · gates<br><i>external-world adapters</i>"]
  domain["domain<br>plan<br><i>domain model</i>"]
  util["util<br>errors · output · parsing · paths<br><i>cross-cutting utilities</i>"]
  config["config<br>settings · toml_io<br><i>configuration</i>"]
  registry["registry<br>agents · teams<br><i>static registries (no deps)</i>"]

  app --> phases --> reporting --> infra --> domain --> util --> config --> registry
```

## What each layer owns

| Layer         | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **app**       | Entry points and the user-facing surface: the PIT loop (`orchestrator`), argparse + subcommands (`cli`), bootstrap (`init`), and the read-only distance report (`how_far`). |
| **phases**    | The business logic of the three sprint phases: Plan, Implement, Test.                                                                                                       |
| **reporting** | Everything written to `autosprint/logs/`, plus the console banners and run summaries.                                                                                       |
| **infra**     | Adapters to the outside world: LLM dispatch, git, test runners, the SQLite mirror, the stop-control file, and gate inspection.                                              |
| **domain**    | The `plan.md` model — `Plan`, `PendingTask`, `CompletedTask`, and the parser/writer.                                                                                        |
| **util**      | Cross-cutting primitives with no business meaning: errors, level-gated output, result parsing, path constants.                                                              |
| **config**    | The `pydantic-settings` singleton and TOML rendering.                                                                                                                       |
| **registry**  | Static data with no internal dependencies: the agent and team definitions.                                                                                                  |

## Why the lazy imports were removed

The original flat layout had three *upward* function-local imports used to break
cycles (`banners → cli`, `plan_phase → cli`, `run_log → implement_phase`). The
refactor eliminated them by moving the shared leaf utilities **down** to where
both sides could reach them:

- gate inspection (`describe_gates`) moved to `infra.gates`
- stop control (`raise_if_stop_between_phases`) moved to `infra.stop`
- refusal detection (`detect_refusal_pattern`) moved to `util.parsing`

The result is zero upward imports anywhere in the package — the static import
graph is a clean DAG, which is exactly what the import-linter contract locks in.

## C4 model

The diagrams below model the system at the three C4 levels. The same
architecture is maintained as code in the LikeC4 model under
[`docs/likec4/`](https://github.com/haakonbull/autosprint/tree/master/docs/likec4),
which can be explored interactively with `just docs likec4 dev`.

### Level 1 — System Context

```{mermaid}
C4Context
  title System Context — Autosprint
  Person(dev, "Developer", "Writes destination.md, reviews plan.md, runs the loop")
  System(autosprint, "Autosprint", "Automated PIT-loop orchestrator")
  System_Ext(target, "Target Repository", "The git repo being worked on")
  System_Ext(claude, "Claude", "Claude Agent SDK + claude CLI")
  System_Ext(copilot, "GitHub Copilot", "Copilot SDK + copilot CLI")

  Rel(dev, autosprint, "Runs commands, reviews plan.md")
  Rel(autosprint, claude, "Dispatches agent prompts")
  Rel(autosprint, copilot, "Dispatches agent prompts")
  Rel(claude, target, "Reads & edits files via tools")
  Rel(copilot, target, "Reads & edits files via tools")
  Rel(autosprint, target, "Runs tests, commits, reverts")
```

### Level 2 — Containers

```{mermaid}
C4Container
  title Container Diagram — Autosprint
  Person(dev, "Developer", "Runs and steers the loop")
  System_Ext(claude, "Claude", "Agent SDK + CLI")
  System_Ext(copilot, "GitHub Copilot", "SDK + CLI")
  System_Ext(target, "Target Repository", "Source, tests, autosprint/")

  Container_Boundary(as, "Autosprint") {
    Container(app, "App / Orchestrator", "Python", "Entry points, CLI, PIT loop")
    Container(phases, "Phases", "Python", "Plan / Implement / Test")
    Container(reporting, "Reporting", "Python", "Logs, stats, banners")
    Container(infra, "Infra", "Python", "Dispatch, git, test runners, db")
    Container(foundation, "Foundation", "Python", "domain · util · config · registry")
  }

  Rel(dev, app, "Runs commands")
  Rel(app, phases, "Drives each sprint")
  Rel(phases, reporting, "Records outcomes")
  Rel(phases, infra, "Dispatch, git, tests")
  Rel(app, infra, "Stop control, gates")
  Rel(infra, foundation, "Config, registries, plan model")
  Rel(infra, claude, "Dispatches prompts")
  Rel(infra, copilot, "Dispatches prompts")
  Rel(infra, target, "Runs tests, commits, reverts")
```

### Level 3 — Components (sprint execution)

```{mermaid}
C4Component
  title Component Diagram — Sprint execution
  Component(orchestrator, "orchestrator", "Python", "Runs the PIT loop")
  ComponentDb(runLog, "run_log", "Python", "Outcomes + escalation")

  Container_Boundary(phases, "Phases") {
    Component(planPhase, "plan_phase", "Python", "Plan + replan")
    Component(implementPhase, "implement_phase", "Python", "Implement + fallback")
    Component(testPhase, "test_phase", "Python", "Test + revert/commit")
  }

  Container_Boundary(infra, "Infra") {
    Component(dispatch, "dispatch", "Python", "LLM dispatch + cache")
    Component(gitOps, "git_ops", "Python", "git commit / restore")
    Component(testRunners, "test_runners", "Python", "pytest / vitest")
  }

  Rel(orchestrator, planPhase, "1. Plan")
  Rel(orchestrator, implementPhase, "2. Implement")
  Rel(orchestrator, testPhase, "3. Test")
  Rel(planPhase, dispatch, "Queries the team")
  Rel(implementPhase, dispatch, "Queries the implementor")
  Rel(testPhase, testRunners, "Runs tests")
  Rel(testPhase, gitOps, "Commits / reverts")
  Rel(implementPhase, runLog, "Logs failures")
```
